```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# Load the data
customers <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Customers.csv")
products <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Products.csv") 
regions <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Regions.csv")
returns <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Returns_1997-1998.csv")
stores <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Stores.csv")
transactions_1997 <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Transactions_1997.csv")
transactions_1998 <- read_csv("data/CSV Files/MavenMarket_Transactions_1998.csv")
```

```{r}
# Data Preperation
# Clean the data
products <- products %>% 
  replace_na(list(recyclable = 0, low_fat = 0)) %>% 
  mutate(gross_profit = product_retail_price - product_cost,
         gross_margin = gross_profit/product_retail_price)

customers <- customers %>% 
  mutate(yearly_income = factor(
                                yearly_income, levels = c("$30K - $50K" , 
                                                          "$70K - $90K"  , 
                                                          "$50K - $70K"  , 
                                                          "$10K - $30K"   ,
                                                          "$90K - $110K" ,
                                                          "$110K - $130K" ,
                                                          "$130K - $150K", 
                                                          "$150K +"  )
                                )
         )

transactions_1997_sales <- transactions_1997 %>%
  left_join(products, by = "product_id") %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  summarise(total_spend_1997 = sum(product_retail_price * quantity))

transactions_1998_sales <- transactions_1998 %>%
  left_join(products, by = "product_id") %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  summarise(total_spend_1998 = sum(product_retail_price * quantity))

customer_sales <- customers %>% 
  left_join(transactions_1997_sales, by = "customer_id") %>% 
  left_join(transactions_1998_sales, by = "customer_id") %>% 
  replace_na(list(total_spend_1997 = 0, total_spend_1998 = 0)) %>%
  mutate(total_spend = total_spend_1997 + total_spend_1998)


```

```{r}
# Customers
customers_city_summary <- customers %>% 
  mutate(married = ifelse(marital_status == "M", 1, 0),
```

```{r}
            total_unique_customers = n_distinct(customer_id),
            total_transactions = n(),
            avg_sales_per_customer = mean(total_sales/n_distinct(customer_id))) %>% 
  mutate(gross_margin = gross_profit/total_sales)
```

```{r}
# Data Visualisation
# member card holders by store
cust_member_card <- customers %>% 
  select(customer_id, member_card) %>%
  left_join(transactions_1998_products, by = "customer_id") %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  summarise(total_spend = sum(product_retail_price), 
            member_card = paste0(first(member_card))) #%>%
  #replace_na(list(total_spend = 0)) 

member_card_agg <- cust_member_card %>%
  group_by(member_card) %>%
  summarise(count_customers = n_distinct(customer_id),
            sum_spend = sum(total_spend, na.rm = T),
            avg_spend = mean(total_spend, na.rm = T),) %>% 
  # arrange by golden, silver, bronze, normal
  mutate(member_card = factor(member_card, levels = c("Golden", "Silver", "Bronze", "Normal"))) %>% 
  arrange(member_card)

cols <- c("Golden" = "gold3", "Silver" = "grey", "Bronze" = "#CE8946", "Normal" = "black")

ggplot(member_card_agg, aes(x = member_card, y = avg_spend, fill = member_card)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Spend by Member Card Tier",
    x = "Member Card",
    y = "Average Spend ($)",
    fill = "Member Card"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_minimal()



# boxplot of spend by member card
ggplot(cust_member_card, aes(x = member_card, y = total_spend, fill = member_card)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Total Spend by Member Card Tier",
       x = "Member Card",
       y = "Total Spend ($)",
       fill = "Member Card") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}

       x = "Occupation",
       y = "Average Spend ($)",

cust_gender_income <- full_cust %>% 
  group_by(gender, yearly_income) %>% 
  summarise(count_customers = n_distinct(customer_id),
            sum_spend = sum(total_spend, na.rm = T),

  arrange(desc(sum_spend))

       y = "Average Spend ($)",
       fill = "Occupation") +
  theme_minimal()
ggplot(cust_gender_income %>% filter(gender == "F"), aes(x = yearly_income, y = avg_spend)) +

  labs(title = "Average Spend by Occupation",
       x = "Occupation",
       y = "Average Spend ($)",
```

```{r}
data <- customer_sales %>%
  mutate(
    birthdate = as.Date(birthdate, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    acct_open_date = as.Date(acct_open_date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    age = round(as.numeric(difftime(as.Date("1998-01-01"), birthdate, units = "days"))/365.25, 0),
    income3050 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$30K - $50K", 1, 0),
     income5070 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$50K - $70K", 1, 0),
     income7090 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$70K - $90K", 1, 0),
     income90110 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$90K - $110K", 1, 0),
     income110130 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$110K - $130K", 1, 0),
     income130150 = ifelse(yearly_income == "$130K - $150K", 1, 0),
     income150plus = ifelse(yearly_income == "$150K +", 1, 0),
    marital_status = as.numeric(factor(marital_status)),
    gender = as.numeric(factor(gender)),
    education = as.numeric(factor(education)),
    member_card = as.numeric(factor(member_card)),
    occupation = as.numeric(factor(occupation)),
    homeowner = as.numeric(factor(homeowner)),
    target_total_spend = as.numeric(total_spend)
  ) %>%
  select(-customer_id, -customer_acct_num, -first_name, -last_name, 
         -customer_address, -customer_city, -customer_state_province, 
         -customer_postal_code, -customer_country, -birthdate, -acct_open_date, -total_spend_1997, -total_spend_1998, -yearly_income, -total_spend)

# Define features and target
X <- data %>% select(-target_total_spend)
y <- ifelse(data$target_total_spend > 50, 1, 0)  # Binary classification: High spenders

# Normalize data
X_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(X))

# Split data into training and testing sets
set.seed(42)
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(customer_sales_knn), 2/3 * nrow(customer_sales_knn))
X_train <- X_scaled[train_indices, ]
X_test <- X_scaled[-train_indices, ]
y_train <- y[train_indices]
y_test <- y[-train_indices]

# Train KNN model on loop
res <- data.frame(nbr_neighbors = 1:100, error_rate_train = 0, error_rate_test = 0)

for (k in 1:100) {
  knn_model <- knn(train = X_train, test = X_train, cl = y_train, k = k)
  res$error_rate_train[k] <- mean(knn_model != y_train)
  
  knn_model <- knn(train = X_train, test = X_test, cl = y_train, k = k)
  res$error_rate_test[k] <- mean(knn_model != y_test)
}

# Plot error rates
ggplot(res, aes(x = nbr_neighbors)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = error_rate_train, color = "Training Error Rate")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = error_rate_test, color = "Testing Error Rate")) +
  labs(title = "Error Rates vs. k", x = "k", y = "Error Rate") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# Evaluate model
confusion_matrix <- table(Predicted = y_pred, Actual = y_test)
confusion_matrix

# best model
best_k <- which.min(res$error_rate_test)
best_k

knn_model_best <- knn(train = X_train, test = X_test, cl = y_train, k = best_k)
```
